title: Nested smart cutoff comparison: equal endpoints
statement:
Let C be an abelian category and L a nonnegative cochain complex. For any integer a with b = a, let g be a map of the indicated cutoffs compatible with their inclusions into the reextended L, and let q satisfy the canonical projection equation below. Then q is a quasi-isomorphism.
theorem verticalCutoff_column_quasiIso_equal
    (L : CochainComplex C ℕ) (a : ℤ)
    (g : (verticalCutoff a).obj L ⟶ (verticalCutoff a).obj L)
    (hg : g ≫ (verticalCutoffι a).app L = (verticalCutoffι a).app L)
    (q : cokernel g ⟶ (verticalWindow a a).obj L)
    (_hq : cokernel.π g ≫ q = HomologicalComplex.restrictionMap
      (CochainComplex.truncLEMap
        (CochainComplex.πTruncGE (L.extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat) a) (a - 1))
      ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat) : QuasiIso q

source.place: Section 12.15, canonical cochain truncations; nested-cutoff specialization by V3.

proof.text: The cutoff inclusion is degreewise monic; cancel it in hg to prove g is identity. Use Mathlib isZero_cokernel_of_epi to identify its cokernel as zero.
Use the simultaneous strict lower support at a and upper support at a-1 to show every window term is zero. The map between zero objects is an isomorphism, hence a quasi-isomorphism.
